items.headline: Heat Advisory issued July 19 at 4:00AM AKDT until July 20 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Hot temperatures as high as 80 degrees expected.

* WHERE...Central Arctic Plains and Western Arctic Plains.

* WHEN...From 10 AM to 10 PM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Individuals not accustomed to these unusually hot
temperatures for this region may experience heat related illnesses.
items.areas: Western Arctic Plains; Central Arctic Plains
items.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids and check up on elderly and vulnerable
relatives and neighbors.

Young children and pets should never be left unattended in vehicles
under any circumstances as vehicle interiors can reach extreme
temperatures in as little as 10 minutes.

Take extra precautions when working in

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued July 19 at 3:57AM AKDT until July 20 at 12:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 35 to 45 mph with gusts up to 65 mph expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp.

* WHEN...Until noon AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
items.areas: Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

items.headline: Flood Watch issued July 19 at 3:51AM AKDT until July 21 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Seward.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A long duration rain event coinciding with an atmospheric
river of moisture moving over the southern Kenai Peninsula
will result in moderate to heavy rain for Seward Saturday
eve
items.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in, or recreating near, areas prone to
flooding should be prepared to take action should flooding develop.

Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 18 at 4:57PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
An atmospheric river of moisture will bring periods of moderate
to heavy rain and gusty southeasterly winds through Turnagain Arm
and across portions of the eastern Kenai Peninsula. The heaviest
rain and strongest winds will likely occur between late tonight
and Monday evening.

Likely (70-80%) rainfall amounts and wind gusts:

For Whittier: 3 to 5 inches of rain; wind gusts up to 35 mph.

For Portage: 2 to 4 inches of rain; wind gusts up to 55 mph.

For Girdwood: 1 to 2 inches of rain; wind gus
items.areas: East Turnagain Arm; Portage; Skilak Lake; Interior Kenai Peninsula; Turnagain Pass; West Prince William Sound & Whittier

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued July 18 at 2:19PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
ESFAFC

* Yentna and Skwentna River basins

* Tonight through Monday Night

Rainfall:

* Widespread rainfall of 1.5 to 2.5 inches of rain is expected in
the western Susitna Valley through Monday Night.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* Expect sharp rises on many small streams and rivers. Crests are
expected to occur on Tuesday for most streams and rivers,
including the Yentna at Lake Creek.
